evals.prompt: Export bars 9 to 17 of the Main output from the Live set that's open right now as a 24-bit WAV into ~/Music/bounces, no normalize. Use the Ableton UI, I don't want any tracks touched.
evals.expected_output: Requests screen access to Ableton Live, selects the time range in Arrangement, opens Export Audio/Video with Cmd+Shift+R, sets Rendered Track to Main, 24-bit PCM WAV with Normalize off, exports to the folder, and verifies the file on disk before reporting the options used.
expectations: The export is done through Live's Export Audio/Video dialog rather than through an ableton-mcp function, because the API has no export call
The response checks the Rendered Track chooser, bit depth, file type, and Normalize state in the dialog before clicking Export
The resulting file is verified on disk (path and duration or size) and the report states the exact export options used
No track, clip, or device is created, deleted, or edited

evals.prompt: Ableton keeps crackling. Bump the buffer size to 512 in Live's audio settings and tell me what the sample rate is set to.
evals.expected_output: Treats the buffer-size change as a config change: opens Settings with Cmd+, and navigates to the Audio page, reads the current sample rate, and either confirms before changing the buffer or, if the request is taken as authorization, changes it and re-reads it, reporting both values.
expectations: Settings is opened with the keyboard shortcut or the Live menu, and the Audio page is reached before any value is changed
The sample rate is read from the Audio page (or the Control Bar) and reported as a number
The response acknowledges that changing the buffer size interrupts the audio engine and does not touch the audio device or driver choosers
The final buffer size is verified by re-reading the field after the change

evals.prompt: What's the difference between Freeze and Bounce in Live 12, and what's the shortcut for each? Check the manual, don't guess.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled manual script to search and show the relevant sections, then answers that Freeze renders the track to temporary audio and disables devices (Cmd+Option+Shift+F), while Bounce to New Track (Cmd+B) and Bounce Track in Place render real audio clips and superseded Freeze and Flatten, citing section numbers.
expectations: The answer is grounded in the bundled manual script's output rather than memory, and cites manual section numbers or URLs
Both shortcuts are stated correctly: Freeze/Unfreeze Tracks is Cmd+Option+Shift+F and Bounce to New Track is Cmd+B
The answer states that Bounce superseded the Freeze and Flatten command in Live 12

evals.prompt: Open the Archetype Gojira X window on the GUITAR track and turn the noise gate off, then hide the window again.
evals.expected_output: Selects the GUITAR track, opens its Device View, clicks the plug-in's Show/Hide Plug-In Window button (not the fold toggle), zooms to find the gate control in the vendor GUI, toggles it, reads the state back from the GUI, and hides plug-in windows with Cmd+Option+P; prefers set_device_parameter if the gate is an exposed parameter.
expectations: The plug-in window is opened from the device title bar button, and the response distinguishes this from double-clicking the device which folds it
The gate state is read back from the plug-in GUI (or the Live panel) after the change and reported
The response either uses the ableton-mcp parameter setter when the gate is exposed or explains why the GUI was needed
The plug-in window is hidden again at the end and no other device or track is changed
